1080	Yes, if he is a Jew, either a physical descendant or a convert, who through his conversion
1081	enters the covenant of Avraham Avinu. A convert cannot convert without fulfilling the mitzvah of
1082	brit milah, and through it he becomes part of the covenant of Avraham Avinu.
1083	So, in these three stories, what do we see?
1084	That HaShem says to the Jew: you want to enter this infinite path
1085	of joining the higher and the lower, joining the limitless with the limited,
1086	joining the level of Divinity above the world with the world, so first of all you must "go forth,"
1087	"Lech Lecha," first of all leave what you are used to.
1088	Second, understand that you have a mission.
1089	You must influence not only yourself, but you must influence the Land.
1090	Go to the Land, come down from the higher place,
1091	from your spiritual ivory tower, and influence reality; turn the land into the Holy Land, into the Land of
1092	Israel.
1093	And in the future the Land of Israel will spread over all the lands.
1094	Or as the well-known saying goes, make Eretz Israel even outside the Land; one must make Eretz Israel through the work of
1095	the Jews.
1096	And afterwards you seal it in the flesh, in an eternal covenant, through which
1097	the eternal union is completed.
1098	So what comes out of this?
1099	It comes out, as we said before, that HaShem is "was, is, and will be" as one.
1100	So with HaShem you cannot ask what is relevant about something that once was; what was, was.
1101	Why can't one ask such a question?
1102	Because what was is the present and is what will be.
1103	Just as what will be is what was.
1104	The limited human being is not in this experience.
1105	But when the Jew understands what Judaism is, as we said, the Torah in our parashah reveals to us
1106	what Judaism is.
1107	What is Judaism?
1108	Judaism is the joining of two opposite matters:
1109	the higher place of "was, is, and will be," which is the higher realms, and the lower place, which is limited reality,
1110	which we called before the reality of the boxes, and the recognition that as a Jew
1111	you can join them in such a way that you do not diminish the revelation of the Infinite, you do not give
1112	it up, and you do not give up the reality of the world.
1113	You do not...
1114	or what is called, nullify the physical and the material.
1115	You manage to find inconceivable ways, through the power of the Infinite
1116	in the soul, in the hidden powers of the soul, to pour
1117	all of the Infinite into reality, and to elevate reality, and bring it
1118	to union with the Infinite of Kadosh Baruch Hu.
1119	But if you want to realize this power, you must understand, first, that it is impossible
1120	to do this without leaving everything you are used to.
1121	Second, understand that it is not "bang, and we're done."
1122	It is not an act of receiving a diploma or a certificate of appreciation on the wall, or being in some status or
1123	other.
1124	You begin a work that is eternal.
1125	Because this work not only never ends, it is also always at the starting stage.
1126	Because toward the Infinite that you are aiming at, you are always only beginning, you are always at the first "Lech Lecha."
1127	Therefore every year we read "Lech Lecha" anew.
1128	That is, you actually go with Kadosh Baruch Hu without any calculations, without
1129	any expectations.
1130	You say to Kadosh Baruch Hu: I am going "to the land that I will show you."
1131	I am truly going to the unknown, for who among us can know the Infinite?
1132	So therefore I go with you in such a way that...
1133	I also accept upon myself that in this journey I do not expect to advance in it,
1134	even though I am advancing in it the most, but I do not expect to progress and tick a box;
1135	I expect the infinite purpose from the very first step,
1136	and I feel at the first step that I have not yet reached the infinite purpose. And what happens when we reach the purpose
1137	of the Infinite?
1138	We do not start from the beginning. There you discover that truly
1139	the Infinite exists.
1140	Truly the Infinite will unite with reality.
1141	So it is an eternal reality.
1142	Let us give a simple analogy.
1143	Can any of us experience infinity?
1144	On the face of it, no.
1145	Everything we do has a beginning and an end.
1146	But notice just one thing.
1147	Every one of us wants to live forever.
1148	What will be in another hundred years?
1149	Will we still want to live forever?
1150	What will be in another thousand years?
1151	What will be in another million years?
1152	What will be in another billion years?
1153	There will be a certain moment.
1154	Is that where it is eternity?
1155	That is, in the inner will for life, there a person can,
1156	in his feeling, in his awareness, feel what eternity is, what infinity is.
1157	Everything has a beginning and an end, but the will for life has no beginning and no end.
1158	Just as it is so in the feeling of the personal self, in the future to come it will be so in the feeling of Kadosh Baruch
1159	Hu.
1160	So we will feel that our desire for Divinity is always, always
1161	only beginning.
1162	After all, each of us feels, like a child, toward his will to live
1163	forever.
1164	And so toward the Infinite that you feel before you, you constantly feel that you are at the starting point.
1165	So we need to take the powers from our parashah, and how to translate them practically into action.
1166	So the Rebbe says here two statements, one a very wonderful statement,
1167	but still not so understandable in its practical side; the second statement is a very practical one.
1168	The first statement: that we understand that we are now in the final stretch, and any moment now
1169	we are going to receive the Promised Land, which includes the Kenites, the Kenizzites, and the Kadmonites.
1170	What will the novelty be now, says the Rebbe?
1171	The novelty now will be that we will not receive it through war and bloodshed, but rather
1172	the nations of the world, of their own good will, will hand over the territory to us.
1173	And today, the Rebbe said this 35 years ago, it sounded detached from reality; today
1174	we already know that we have received parts of Syria without a war.
1175	And so?
1176	Why do only we understand this?
1177	Not only we understand it; anyone who observes understands it.
1178	But any moment now we are going to receive all ten lands,
1179	as they say, on a silver platter.
1180	But what is the Rebbe telling us?
1181	He says we must begin making the preparations to receive these lands.
1182	That is, each and every one of us must truly... and again I said, the Rebbe does not close the matter
1183	and open an opening here.
1184	He throws out here, so to speak, a very powerful statement into the air, but he leaves
1185	us to reflect on what it means that we must make actual preparations to receive these lands
1186	from the good will of the nations of the world.
1187	The second thing the Rebbe says, and he focuses us more on a concrete matter, the Rebbe
1188	says that a Jew must do "Lech Lecha" in the study of Torah.
1189	That is, we said before, what is the essence of "Lech Lecha"?
1190	To leave what was until today and go toward something
1191	completely new.
1192	So too in the study of Torah.
1193	Not to hold on to or rely on what I already know, that I have learned Torah and already keep Torah
1194	and mitzvot, but to feel that everything until today is limited.
1195	It is according to the powers that I recognize within me.
